extraction_report.paper_summary: USHER: an EM-style framework that uses Fused Gromov–Wasserstein optimal transport + entropic filtering to infer correspondences between out-of-distribution (OOD) and reference foundation-model embeddings, then fits a low-complexity transform (linear/MLP) to map OOD embeddings back to the reference embedding space. Demonstrated on scGPT embeddings (Xenium → scRNA-seq) and H-optimus-1 histopathology embeddings (post-MALDI → post-PCF).
extraction_report.research_objective: Enable post-hoc calibration of foundation-model embeddings so OOD data (new assays/protocols) are mapped into the model's native representation, preserving downstream compatibility without fine-tuning the foundation model.
identified_experiments: Xenium (spatial transcriptomics) → scRNA-seq alignment for scGPT embeddings (Fig. 2, Sec. 3.1)
Post-MALDI → post-PCF H&E histopathology alignment for H-optimus-1 embeddings (Fig. 4, Sec. 3.2)
Held-out-sample transfer/generalization test (apply fitted USHER to additional Xenium sections, Fig. 3)
Gene/protein imputation downstream tasks after alignment (imputation via nearest neighbors; protein regression)
